name: Yangban
description: The hereditary aristocratic class of Joseon Korea that monopolized official posts and land through the Confucian civil-service examinations. Collapsed with the abolition of the class system under Japanese rule.

name: Hwarang
description: An elite youth warrior order of the Silla kingdom, blending martial training with Buddhist and Confucian moral cultivation. Central to Silla's unification of the Korean peninsula.

name: Devaraja (God-King)
description: The divine-kingship office of the Khmer Empire, in which the ruler was identified with a deity and legitimized by monumental temple-mountains such as Angkor Wat. Coordinated the irrigation systems that sustained the empire.

name: Mongol Khan
description: The elected supreme ruler of the Mongol Empire, chosen at a kurultai and bound by the yassa legal code. Commanded the largest contiguous land empire in history via a decimal army and the yam courier relay.

name: Sogdian Merchant
description: Iranian-speaking merchants of Sogdiana who dominated Silk Road trade between China and the West. Their caravan networks also transmitted Buddhism, Manichaeism, and writing systems across Central Asia.

name: Mesopotamian Scribe
description: The cuneiform scribes who produced the earliest written records of humanity — contracts, tax accounts, and literature. Trained in the edubba school, they formed a literate elite at the core of Mesopotamian temple and palace administration.

name: Aksumite King (Negus)
description: The monarch of the Aksumite Empire, a major Red Sea trading power and among the first states to adopt Christianity. Issued its own coinage and erected monumental stelae.

name: Griot / Jali
description: Hereditary oral historians, musicians, and praise-singers of the Mande peoples of West Africa. As living archives, they preserved royal genealogies and epics such as Sundiata for centuries before writing.

name: Quipucamayoc
description: Specialists of the Inca Empire who encoded census, tribute, and historical data on quipu — knotted cords using a positional decimal system. A bureaucratic memory apparatus that functioned entirely without writing.
functions: recorded census and tribute on quipu

name: Chasqui Runner
description: Highly trained relay runners of the Inca Empire who carried messages and goods along the 40,000-km Qhapaq Ñan road network. Teams at tambo posts relayed information across the Andes in days.

name: Maya Scribe
description: Literate elite specialists of the Classic Maya who composed hieroglyphic texts recording dynastic histories, astronomy, and ritual on stone monuments and bark-paper codices. Their script is the most complete writing system of the pre-Columbian Americas.

name: Vestal Virgin
description: Priestesses of Vesta who tended Rome's sacred hearth, on whose purity the city's fate was believed to depend. Held unusual legal autonomy in a deeply patriarchal society.

name: Janissary
description: The elite standing infantry of the Ottoman Empire, originally recruited through the devshirme levy of Christian boys. Among Europe's first professional gunpowder armies; disbanded by force in 1826.

name: Mamluk
description: Enslaved soldiers, mostly Turkic and Circassian, who rose to become the ruling military elite of Egypt. Defeated the Mongols at Ain Jalut in 1260 and ruled a sultanate until the 16th century.

name: Viking Raider
description: Seaborne Norse warriors who raided, traded, and settled from Ireland to the Caspian and reached North America. The longship's shallow draft made their mobility decisive.

name: Scholar-Official (Shidafu)
description: The Confucian scholar-bureaucrats selected by the imperial examinations who administered China for over a millennium. Fused political office with moral and literary authority.
